subject: When the bedtime routine meets the bed
preheader: The practical questions between getting into bed, settling and getting up again.
intro: A bedtime routine can be well considered and still be difficult to carry out. Getting comfortable, repositioning or managing a transfer may be the part that needs a closer look.

Sleep hygiene includes habits and environment. In an equipment assessment, it is also worth asking whether the person can carry out that wind-down routine with the bed access, comfort and assistance available.
sectionTitle: What needs to work through the night?
body: Consider three moments: the first transfer into bed, any repositioning overnight, and getting up in the morning. What is easy, what needs help and what interrupts the routine?
Sleep Choice can help you explore a bed and mattress configuration through a seven-night in-home trial, with those questions guiding what the person and support team observe.
Equipment is one part of the picture. It does not replace your wider assessment of sleep or the person's clinical needs.
actionTitle: Bring the question, not a finished equipment list
actionText: Reply with a short, de-identified outline of what is difficult in the night-time routine. We can talk through the equipment questions and a possible trial.
trialFooterText: Sleep Choice offers seven-night in-home bed and mattress trials.
